title: The delivery fact has no home in rwb-litigation and no published operation on any of the three services it crosses
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-002, story, data table, endpoints table); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-02; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.2; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.1 and T-A.1; _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: 2 tables, 5 operations, 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow)
section: RWB-S4-E5002-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8, 13, 19; RWB-S4-E5002-CON sections 1, 2, 3, 7 (AC2, AC3), 8 (BR3, BR10), 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8, 13, 19; the metadata rows and the two fragments
description: Five values the step needs are fixed by no source. (1) The home of the delivery fact: FEAT-LIT-02 says the step reads the WIN proof of delivery from v_ace_pod and writes it onto the notice, but the ownership rows of rwb-litigation name only hearing and legal_action as its tables, and neither carries served_result or delivered_at; the notice row DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023 is rwb-comms'. (2) The grant of the ACE read: rwb-litigation holds no v_ace_* grant, so the v_ace_pod read cannot be the service's own. (3) The element of v_ace_pod: no source read for this key lists its fields and no field identifier is published for it, while the legacy data table lists v_ace_customer and not v_ace_pod. (4) The served-result field of the notice: its identifier is not in any source, and the legacy table names only six of the nine notice fields. (5) The interface: of the five owned operations of rwb-litigation none records a delivery, and the legacy endpoints table names only the legal-action create and the notice approve; no operation of rwb-source-data, rwb-comms or rwb-case for this fact is named anywhere. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the step needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Context pack: 'Tables (2) hearing, legal_action', 'REST operations provided (5) GET/PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, POST /legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings, POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve', 'Events (0)', 'Jobs (0)', 'Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow'. TSD S4 T3.1 gives legal_action 14 fields (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing 6 (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029), none of them a served result or a delivery date; T-A.1 gives the five operations above and no delivery operation. The legacy data table names recovery_case, timer, v_ace_customer, notice, decision_log_entry and rule_row; the legacy endpoints table names POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions and POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve. Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-02: 'Reads the WIN proof of delivery from v_ace_pod, which ACE ingests, and writes it onto the notice; the notice period timer starts from it', systems 'ACE (ingested from WIN)'. FSD S4 A2.2.2 gives integration points 'WIN' and no interface.
area: Application and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P1 rwb-source-data and P6 rwb-comms
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P1 rwb-source-data and P6 rwb-comms architects
proposed: Carry the legacy sentences unchanged with their origin tags and record the target reading: the proof arrives on rwb-source-data's ACE-data contract for v_ace_pod (one hop, 2 s, faked, operation name left as the placeholder); the notice and its served result are read on rwb-comms' contract (operation name left as the placeholder); this service writes no business row, its only durable effects being the decision record, the workflow state and the notice-period timer; and no sixth operation is added to the five of TSD S4 T-A.1.

title: The proof of delivery is named as an event in the rules and the FSD, while the service publishes and consumes nothing and the case answer has no operation name
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 (event column PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED, PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED, DELIVERY_FAILED); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows: Events (0); Temporal and Drools slides that name this service, slide 7 notes naming EV-15 and the 7-day proof window); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.2.4.4 (system background events None); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T4, T5.3
section: RWB-S4-E5002-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.8, 13; RWB-S4-E5002-CON sections 2, 3, 7 (AC4, AC6), 8 (BR4), 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 19; the events_published and events_consumed keys of both fragments
description: Two readings of the trigger collide. The Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 names an event for each of the three rules and the Temporal design names EV-15 proof of delivery, which reads as an event or a message on a topic. Against that, the ownership rows of rwb-litigation give the service zero events, the FSD A2.2.4.4 declares no system background event for the feature, and DP-09 (outbox and inbox) and DP-14 (topic naming) are not in the pattern set of this key, so the service has no inbox, no consumer group and no published event to name. Separately, the answer that asks rwb-case to move the case, to start the case-stage timer and to raise the officer task has no operation name in any source: TSD S4 T5.2 says only 'P3 for the case'.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lines 146 to 148: R-LIT-07 event PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED, R-LIT-08 PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED, R-LIT-09 DELIVERY_FAILED, each with systems 'WIN and DMS, Workbench'. Context pack slide 7 notes: 'Proof of delivery (EV-15) starts the notice-period timer (R-LIT-07); the proof window is 7 days'. Context pack ownership rows: 'Events (0) - None'. FSD S4 A2.2.4.4: 'None - No background event'. TSD S4 T5.3: 'Events - None'. TSD S4 T5.2: 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log ...'. The metadata rows of both stories carry Contract, Integration and External dependencies None, and the patterns applied are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only.
area: Integration and trigger design, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case and P6 rwb-comms
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case and P6 rwb-comms architects and the event platform team
proposed: Read PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED, PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED and DELIVERY_FAILED as the names of workflow signals and not as Kafka subscriptions: the proof arrives on the P1 contract and the case stage is answered on the rwb-case contract, both one hop with a 2 s budget, and neither story publishes or consumes an event. Name the case read and the case-stage answer in the rwb-case contract story when it is written, and leave the metadata rows as the plan gives them.

title: The notice-period timer has no stated home and the notice period has no value in any source
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-LIT-07 (timer column 'Notice period by product and type') and R-LIT-08 ('7 days'); _work/msr/context/S4.md (Jobs (0); Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow; Temporal and Drools slide 7 notes); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E5-002 data table (timer, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T5.3 and T6
section: RWB-S4-E5002-APP sections 2, 3, 6, 12.5, 12.6, 13 and 15; RWB-S4-E5002-CON sections 2, 3, 7 (AC1, AC6), 11, 12.6, 13 and 19
description: The legacy story starts the notice period from delivered_at and its data table names a timer row, which in the target is P3's table. The pack gives rwb-litigation no job and one workflow, so the clock can only be a durable timer of LitigationWorkflow, but no source states that the notice period timer belongs to S4 rather than to the case service. Its duration is worse: R-LIT-07 gives the timer as 'Notice period by product and type' with no number, no list and no reference table, while the 7-day proof window of R-LIT-08 is a value. The officer task that R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 raise has the same problem in reverse: the task row DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026 is P3's and no source says how the request crosses to rwb-case.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-07 timer column 'Notice period by product and type', R-LIT-08 '7 days', R-LIT-09 '2 working days'. Context pack: 'Jobs (0) - None', 'Workflows (1) - LitigationWorkflow', Temporal and Drools slide 7: 'Temporal keeps the dates ... Notice period starts on proof of delivery'. Legacy data table: 'timer | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036'. TSD S4 T5.3 gives no event and T6 gives no scheduler; the FSD A2.3.2 gives the notice-period feature the integration points 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler', which the target replaces with Temporal.
area: Workflow and reference data, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case architect and the business owner of the notice period
proposed: Declare the proof window of 7 days and the notice period as two durable timers of LitigationWorkflow, the first started at dispatch and the second at delivered_at under R-LIT-07; read the notice period as a versioned reference row per product and notice type, carry its content as the placeholder until the business owner publishes it, hold the timer and answer no move when the row is missing, and keep the case-stage timer and the officer task rows with rwb-case on the stage outcome.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-002, so both stories trace to the feature and one module requirement
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-002 (metadata table rows Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-02, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-DRI-17, Decision - no requirement row); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-002 with reqs = []; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-02; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010)
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories and the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-002 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-02 and the prerequisite FEAT-DRI-17 and no requirement row, the run's legacy index records an empty requirement list, and the Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. The FSD S4 requirements table has no requirement that names the proof of delivery on its own; the nearest is REQ-S4-001, 'Demand and recall notices are generated by rule, approved, dispatched, and their notice periods are timed', which covers the notice period this story starts. Both stories therefore trace to FEAT-LIT-02 and to REQ-S4-001 with the reading stated, and the PRD column carries the placeholder until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD of the module adds an identifier.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-002 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 and none of them names a proof of delivery; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-02 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind System, primary role 'Runs unattended', systems 'ACE (ingested from WIN)', depends on FEAT-DRI-17 and no requirement.
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Add one requirement row to the Epics 3 to 8 PRD and to the S4 module trace covering the proof of delivery as the start of the notice period, and rewrite the requirement column of both stories and of their fragments when it exists; until then keep REQ-S4-001 with the reading stated in section 18.

title: The rule package that decides the three rules is a consumed contract of another service with no dependency row and no pattern in the set
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09; _work/msr/context/S4.md (DP table row DP-04 and the rule governance block of Temporal and Drools slide 11); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.2.3.1; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5002-APP and RWB-S4-E5002-CON (Contract dependencies None; patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19)
section: RWB-S4-E5002-APP sections 3, 4, 8, 12.2, 12.8, 13 and 19; RWB-S4-E5002-CON sections 3, 7 (AC6), 8 (BR11), 12.2, 12.8 and 19
description: The step cannot decide anything without the LITIGATION package of rwb-decision at its version in force, because the three rules and the served-result check are rows of that package. In the target the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and the runtime is embedded per service, which the DP table carries as DP-04 with H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON. DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key, no such platform or service contract story is in the dependencies the plan gives this slice, and the metadata rows say Contract dependencies None, so the package read is a consumed contract that no row declares.
evidence: Context pack DP table: 'DP-04 embedded Drools + rule packages from rwb-decision', full table row 'DP-04 ... H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON'; Temporal and Drools slide 11: 'RULE GOVERNANCE (rwb-decision, P7) Rule models + central ledger, approve, publish EV-30, seal decision records'. FSD S4 A2.2.3.1 gives R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09 and BR-S4-002 'read from reference data with its version'. The patterns of both stories are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19; the dependency rows of both stories are None except the app story's three H rows.
area: Dependency map and rule governance, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision and the platform rule kit
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision architect and the platform rule-kit owner
proposed: Carry the package read as a non-blocking consumed row on rwb-decision's contract with its fake, keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them, and record DP-04 with its two contracts in the Dependency Map when the rule-governance keys are realigned; the embedded runtime stays a service-template capability and no rule row is authored in this key.
